column2: A Town Is Born

Pilgrims, pedlars and stonemasons have followed the roads to the [target_wonder.GetName] for fifty years, and now some of them will not leave. Tents have become huts, the huts have become houses with tile roofs, and a market is held under the walls every Wellentag. The reeve of [target_province.GetName] asks whether this new town may stand.
Let them stay. [target_province.GetName] grows with them.
Burn the huts and take their goods. The wonder needs no hangers-on.
[target_wonder.GetName]

My scribes have all but moved into the [target_wonder.GetName]. They come back with ink to their elbows and armfuls of copied passages, old maps and the sayings of sages long dead, and the pages they lay before me tonight are better than anything they wrote before.
Let them read everything on its shelves.
Your scribes work in the [target_wonder.GetName], and your book will be the finer for it.
The Fountain of Youth

The fountain at the heart of the [target_wonder.GetName] is fed by a spring the gardeners swear has never run dry. I kneel at its rim and lower a silver cup into the water. It is cold enough to hurt my teeth, and as I drink, a warmth spreads from my chest to my fingertips. When I rise my knees do not ache. For the first time in years they do not ache.

The fountain is laughing at me. I can hear it! So I laugh back and leap in, clothes and all, and I swallow the water by the mouthful until I choke on it. The gardeners drag me out by my collar. My bones creak, my eyes are dim, and my reflection in the pool is an old [Root.GetManWoman]'s face. The fountain has stopped laughing. I have not.

The fountain at the heart of the [target_wonder.GetName] is a poor cousin of the Pools I found in the jungles of Lustria, but the water carried from there still sings in its basin. I know now how it must be taken: slowly, without fear, letting it fill the lungs before the throat. The cold bites and then the warmth comes, deeper than any gardener has ever felt it. Years slip away from me like a cloak.
Drank the free waters of Ganaina too recently: the youth of one decade cannot be taken twice. Wait until §Y[Root.10yr_fountain_timer.GetExpiryDate]§!
The years fall away.
I have never felt so old!
An Evening at the Tavern

Lamplight and loud voices spill from the tavern in the shadow of the [target_wonder.GetName]. [drinking_buddy.GetTitledFirstName] takes me by the arm. "You have the face of a [Root.GetManWoman] who has read too many tax rolls. One night, my friend. The ale here is brewed by the monks of the wonder and it would be a sin to let it go to waste."
Lead the way, and keep the cups coming!
Some who drink here never quite stop...
One cup, and then I would rather we talked.
One More Round

Since that first night I have gone back to the tavern by the [target_wonder.GetName] more often than I like to admit. The innkeeper knows my cup, the minstrel knows my favourite song, and my servants have learned to fetch me home before dawn.
Pour me another!
Deadly Traps

Curiosity has always killed more courtiers than the plague. [target_courtier.GetTitledName] and [target_courtier_2.GetTitledName] went into the deep vaults of the [target_wonder.GetName] with a lantern and a map they bought from a grave robber. The stones closed behind them. When the masons broke through two days later they found what the blades and the pit had left. [old_owner.GetTitledFirstName] built well.
Curse you, [old_owner.GetFirstName]!

Word comes from my old [target_wonder.GetName]: the traps I had laid in its depths still bite. [target_courtier.GetTitledName] and [target_courtier_2.GetTitledName] of [FROM.GetTitledFirstName]'s court went looking for my treasures and found my blades instead.
Ha! Let them enjoy their prize.

[target_vassal.GetTitledName],

The [target_wonder.GetName] is spoken of in every hall of my realm, and travellers who come to my court ask to see it before they ask to see me. You have kept it well. I wanted you to know that I have noticed.

[target_liege.GetTitledFirstName]
It is all thanks to my liege's guidance.
I have done well, haven't I?

My liege,

The [target_wonder.GetName] brings pilgrims, trade and glory to my lands, and I have never forgotten that I hold it under your protection. Thank you for your kind words.

[target_vassal.GetTitledFirstName]
A loyal vassal is worth a wonder.
Crumbling Stone

A carved stone the size of an ox has fallen from the [target_wonder.GetName] and smashed into the square below, missing a goose girl by a hand's breadth. The master mason says the mortar is a century old and tired, and that there will be more where that came from unless the scaffolds go up.
Raise the scaffolds. It will stand another hundred years.
Collectors will pay well for pieces of the [target_wonder.GetName]...
A Harvest from [target_province.GetName]

The keepers of the [target_wonder.GetName] send word that their stores are full. The gardeners have cut rare herbs from the beds, and the miners have brought up ore from the deep shafts that no smith in the province can name.
I will take the herbs.
I will take the ore.

[Root.GetBookThemeCap] by the famous [Root.GetAuthorTitle] [Root.GetAuthorName], thought lost for centuries, found in a far-off court and bought by [Root.GetTitledName] for the library.
Once thought to be [Root.GetBookThemeWithArticle] by the famous [Root.GetAuthorTitle] [Root.GetAuthorName]. The ink was too fresh, the vellum too white, and the scholars now call it a clever forgery.

The scholars of the land came to the library of [Root.GetTitledName] and agreed that the lost [Root.GetBookTheme] by the [Root.GetAuthorTitle] [Root.GetAuthorName] was true, and the copyists began their work that very night.
The Lost Book

A merchant fresh from [book_province.GetName] swears by every god he knows that he has seen it with his own eyes: [Root.GetBookThemeWithArticle] by the famous [Root.GetAuthorTitle] [Root.GetAuthorName], a work the scholars of my library have mourned as lost for centuries. It lies in a strongbox in the realm of [book_province_holder.GetTitledName], and its owner may be persuaded to part with it.\n\nThe road is long and the purse must be heavy. Whom shall I send?
[possible_emissary1.GetTitledFirstName] has the patience for it.
[possible_emissary2.GetTitledFirstName] knows the roads.
Not now. Perhaps the book will wait for me.
Enough of dusty old books.
You will never again be offered a lost book.
A Death on the Road

The servants of [emissary.GetTitledFirstName] have come back without their master. Fever, bandits or beastmen, they cannot agree which, but [emissary.GetSheHe] lies in a roadside grave far from home. They bring back what was left in the purse, and no book.
May the gods keep [emissary.GetHerHim].
Only a Rumour

[emissary.GetTitledFirstName] is back, dusty and sour. There was no book. The strongbox held a merchant's ledgers, and the merchant had never heard of [Root.GetAuthorName]. Somewhere a tavern teller is laughing at us. [emissary.GetSheHeCap] hands back what is left of the purse.
A wasted journey.

My [Root.GetLordLady],

I have found the book, and it is everything we hoped. But its owner knows it too, and will not let it go for the sum we agreed. Fifty pieces of gold more and it is ours. Without them I must come home empty-handed.

Your faithful servant,
[emissary.GetFirstName]
Send the gold.
Come home. No book is worth that.
The Emissary Is Gone
No book has come, and no letter. Word has reached me at last: [emissary.GetTitledFirstName] was seen in a port tavern, buying wine for strangers with my gold, and then took ship for parts unknown.
Thief! May [emissary.GetSheHe] drown.
Send men after [emissary.GetHerHim]. Quiet men.
Hired knives will hunt the thief.
The Hunt

The men I sent have come back. They found [emissary.GetTitledFirstName] in a boarding house by the docks, and [emissary.GetSheHe] will steal nothing more. Of my gold, they say, there was nothing left.
The men I sent have come back with nothing but excuses. [emissary.GetTitledFirstName] saw them coming and got away, and worse, one of them was taken and talked. People are asking who sent them.
Justice is done.
Fools!
The Book Is Found

[emissary.GetTitledFirstName] is home, and from the saddlebags comes a bundle of oilcloth. Inside is [Root.GetBookThemeWithArticle] by the famous [Root.GetAuthorTitle] [Root.GetAuthorName]. The binding is cracked and the pages smell of old smoke, but the hand is fine and the words are as the old scholars quoted them.\n\nOr so it seems.
I will read it myself.
Call the scholars of the land to judge it.
Put it with the other treasures of the library.
A Forgery

A scholar who came to see the [Root.GetAuthorName] book asked to look at it in daylight, then asked for a lens, then went white. The ink, [book_scholar.GetSheHe] says, is oak-gall of a kind no scribe used before the last century, and the vellum was aged with tea. The book is a forgery, and [book_scholar.GetSheHe] has already said so in front of half the court.
Throw this slanderer in the dungeon.
An honest scholar is worth more than a false book. Stay with us.
The Ink Is Too Fresh

Night after night I have read the [Root.GetBookTheme] of [Root.GetAuthorName], and something is wrong. The book quotes a writer who was born after its author died, and in the margin of one page a careless forger has left a thumbprint in ink that still smears. I have paid a fortune for a fake.
At least I learned something, even if it was not what I paid for.
Into the fire with it!
The Gathering of Scholars

They came from every court within a month's ride: grey-bearded scholars, sharp-eyed young copyists, a priest of Verena with a lens on a chain. For three days they argued over the [Root.GetBookTheme] in the reading hall of the library, and on the fourth they agreed. It is true. It is the lost work of [Root.GetAuthorName], and it is mine.

They came from every court within a month's ride, and it took them a single afternoon. The binding is new leather rubbed with soot, the hand is wrong, and the forger misspelled the name of [Root.GetAuthorName] on the last page. Still, the argument that followed was the finest the library has seen, and the scholars went home talking of my hospitality.
Let the copyists begin.
Well, it was a good debate.
A Tomb Under the Works

The foreman of the works at the [target_wonder.GetName] has come to me with clay to his knees. While digging the foundations his men broke into a sealed chamber: a tomb, old beyond reckoning, with carvings no one can read and a stone door still shut.\n\nThe diggers will not go back down until I tell them what to do. Some of them are saying the dead should be left alone.
Open it. Carefully.
I will see to the opening myself.
Seal it again. Let the dead sleep.
Do not trouble me with every hole in the ground.
The workers may find something of value, or nothing at all. Old tombs are not always safe.
With someone who knows the old ways at hand there will be no accident, and a better chance of finding something.
You will not hear of tombs found by your builders again.

The stone door would not open, so the foreman had the lintel pried loose. The roof of the tomb came down with it. Six men are dead under the rubble, and the rest are muttering about curses and refuse to go near the place.
The tomb was empty. Robbers found it long ago and left nothing but bones, dust and a few broken pots.
Behind the door lay a warrior on a bier of stone, and around him the goods he was buried with: rings, cups and coins of a mint no one remembers. Not a king's treasure, but a fair sum.

The tomb was a lord's, and his heirs did not stint. Gold plate, jewelled torcs and chests of old coin lay around the bier, untouched for a thousand years. The workers stare at it as if it might vanish.

The tomb belonged to someone great. Beside the bones, beneath centuries of dust, lay a treasure fit for a king, untouched since the day the door was sealed, and around it grave goods enough to make a merchant weep.
Bury the dead and get back to work.
Pay their families well.
It is my ground, so it is my treasure.
Share it with the men who found it.
The treasure is yours whatever you choose.
The armour of a forgotten champion, found on the bier of an old tomb under the foundations of a great work.
A blade buried with a forgotten champion, found in an old tomb under the foundations of a great work. It is still sharp.
A sceptre set with emeralds, taken from the bones of a king whose name no chronicle remembers.

The smith I hired has seen my armoury and says there is no need to bring in strangers: the forges here are as fine as any in the realm, and the master of the armoury can do the work. What shall it make?
A sword.
A zweihander, the greatsword of the Empire.
A scimitar.
A lance.
An axe.
A mace.
A bow.
A suit of armour.
The master of the armoury has finished. [From.GetSheHeCap] lays the work on the table before me, still smelling of oil and the forge, and steps back to watch my face.
Fine work.
Made in the armoury of [Root.GetTitledName] by its own master smith.

I took [target_character.GetTitledName] down to the lower levels of my wonder, past the racks, the cages and the things in jars, and let [target_character.GetHerHim] have a good long look. [target_character.GetSheHeCap] has gone very quiet.

I took [target_character.GetTitledName] down to the lower levels of my wonder, past the racks, the cages and the things in jars. [target_character.GetSheHeCap] has seen worse, by the look of it, and is studying the instruments with interest.
It would be a shame if you ended up down here.
I am sure you will remember this place when I need a favour.
Fine work, is it not? Let me show you the rest.
Ha! Your face! It is only a museum, my friend.
[target_character.GetSheHeCap] may take it as a threat instead.
[target_character.GetSheHeCap] may take it as a threat instead.
[target_character.GetTitledName] laughed in my face. [target_character.GetSheHeCap] asked whether I keep these toys to frighten children, and told the story at supper to everyone who would listen.
Laugh while you can.

[FromFrom.GetTitledName] has invited me to a private meeting at the [target_wonder.GetName], away from the eyes and ears of the court. [FromFrom.GetSheHeCap] does not say what [FromFrom.GetSheHe] wishes to discuss.
I will come.
I have no time for this.
Send my regrets, with every courtesy.

[From.GetTitledName] has come to the [target_wonder.GetName]. The servants have withdrawn, the doors are shut and we are alone among the hedges and fountains. No one will hear what is said here, or what is done.
Let us talk, as friends.
Let us forget the world for an hour.
At last, my love, we are alone.
No one will hear [From.GetHerHim] scream.
[From.GetSheHeCap] may become your lover.
[From.GetSheHeCap] is unlikely to welcome your advances.
An hour together may lift your cares and deepen your love.
Has the cunning or the nature for murder
You will try to kill [From.GetHerHim]. It may go wrong.
[From.GetTitledName] has [From.GetPoliteRefuse] refused my invitation to the [target_wonder.GetName].
So be it.
[From.GetTitledName] and I walked for an hour in the [target_wonder.GetName], and talked of the realm, of old wars and of the people we both know. [From.GetSheHeCap] has a way with words.
A remarkable [From.GetManWoman]. I am thoroughly impressed.
A pleasant hour. I think well of [From.GetHerHim].
Pleasant enough, I suppose.
[From.GetTitledName] seemed pleased with our meeting at the [target_wonder.GetName].
In the quiet of the [target_wonder.GetName], [From.GetTitledName] has taken my hand and made it very plain what [From.GetSheHe] wants of me.
I want you too.
Tonight, and nothing more.
How dare you!
Come closer, then. Closer.
You become lovers.
One night, and no promises.
[From.GetTitledName] did not pull [From.GetHerHis] hand away. We stayed in the [target_wonder.GetName] until the candles burned out, and when we parted at dawn it was as lovers.
[From.GetTitledName] stayed the night with me in the [target_wonder.GetName], and was gone before dawn without a word of what comes next.
Life is good.
I want more of [From.GetHerHim].
[From.GetTitledName] and I spent the whole evening alone in the [target_wonder.GetName]. For a few hours there was no realm, no court and no one watching.
If only it could always be like this.
[From.GetTitledName] pulled away from me as if I were a leper, and left the [target_wonder.GetName] without a word. By morning the whole court knew.
[From.GetSheHeCap] will regret this.
We were alone in the [target_wonder.GetName] when [From.GetTitledName] drew a knife. There is no one to call and nowhere to hide.
I leaned in close to [From.GetTitledName], and saw the knife in [From.GetHerHis] hand a heartbeat too late.
Run!
Fight!
You may get away unhurt.
You may get away wounded.
You may not get away at all.
You may kill [From.GetHerHim].
[From.GetSheHeCap] may kill you.
I ran, and I did not stop running until I was among my guards. I am alive, and unhurt, and I will never set foot in that place again.
I got away, but not before the blade found me. The physicians have stitched the wound, and say I was lucky.
I will not forget this.
The blade went deep. The fountains are red, the stars are going out, and no one is coming.
[From.GetTitledName] got away, and by now the whole court will know what I tried to do.
[From.GetTitledName] got away with a wound, and by now the whole court will know what I tried to do.
Next time.
[From.GetTitledName] is dead, and there is no one to say how it happened but me.
We fought among the hedges like animals, and only one of us walked out. [From.GetTitledName] lies in the fountain.
It was [From.GetHerHim] or me.
The Last Rest
[From.GetTitledName] is dead, and the realm's great burial ground in the [target_wonder.GetName] waits for [From.GetHerHim]. How shall my predecessor be laid to rest?

[From.GetTitledName] is dead. The priests of Morr have come to ask how [From.GetSheHe] is to be laid in the [target_wonder.GetName]: with a procession of black-robed mourners and a hundred candles, or with a single prayer and a plain stone.

[From.GetTitledName] is dead. The tomb in the [target_wonder.GetName] stands open, and the Ancestors wait to receive [From.GetHerHim]. The Lorekeepers ask how much of the hold's gold shall go into the grave with [From.GetHerHim], as is proper.

[From.GetTitledName] is dead, and the embalmers have already begun. They ask how rich the tomb in the [target_wonder.GetName] shall be: what gold, what servants, what wards against the robbers of later ages.

[From.GetTitledName] is dead, and the gods watch to see how [From.GetHerHis] successor honours [From.GetHerHim]. The [target_wonder.GetName] is ready for the skulls of the sacrifices. How many shall there be?

[From.GetTitledName] is dead. The tomb in the [target_wonder.GetName] has been washed and the shroud is ready. The holy men ask how great a gathering shall see [From.GetHerHim] to [From.GetHerHis] rest.
The greatest funeral the realm has ever seen.
A funeral fitting for [From.GetHerHim].
The cheapest. The dead do not care.
[From.GetSheHeCap] deserves no burial at all.
A grand funeral will follow. Those who loved the dead will be grateful, those who hated them offended.
A fitting funeral will follow. Those who loved the dead will be grateful.
Those who loved the dead will be angry, those who hated them pleased.
The funeral of [FromFrom.GetTitledName] is over. The realm came to see [FromFrom.GetHerHim] laid in the [target_wonder.GetName], and the grief, real or not, was loud.[Root.GetBigBurialHaterSentence]

The black procession wound through the city for a whole day before [FromFrom.GetTitledName] was laid in the [target_wonder.GetName]. The priests of Morr sang, the bells tolled, and the ravens sat quiet on the roofs.[Root.GetBigBurialHaterSentence]

[FromFrom.GetTitledName] has been laid in the [target_wonder.GetName] beside [FromFrom.GetHerHis] ancestors, with axe and rune-plate and the gold that is [FromFrom.GetHerHis] due. The Lorekeepers have written the name in the Book of Remembering.[Root.GetBigBurialHaterSentence]

The embalmers did their work well. [FromFrom.GetTitledName] lies wrapped in linen and gold in the [target_wonder.GetName], and the door has been sealed with every ward the priests know. In a thousand years [FromFrom.GetSheHe] will look much the same.[Root.GetBigBurialHaterSentence]

The pyres burned for three nights at the [target_wonder.GetName]. The skulls of the sacrifices have been stacked around the bones of [FromFrom.GetTitledName], and the warband feasted until no one could stand.[Root.GetBigBurialHaterSentence]

[FromFrom.GetTitledName] was carried to the [target_wonder.GetName] before sunset, as is proper, and the whole court followed in white. The holy men read from the scriptures until the stars came out.[Root.GetBigBurialHaterSentence]
Rest well.
The realm will remember how the dead were honoured.
\n\nThose who hated [FromFrom.GetHerHim] are less pleased, and say the gold could have been better spent.
The shrine in my wonder is ready to receive a holy relic. I have one worthy of it: [target_artifact_1.GetName].
The shrine in my wonder is ready to receive a holy relic. Which of mine shall it be: [target_artifact_1.GetName] or [target_artifact_2.GetName]?
The shrine in my wonder is ready to receive a holy relic. Which of mine shall it be: [target_artifact_1.GetName], [target_artifact_2.GetName] or [target_artifact_3.GetName]?
[target_artifact_1.GetName].
[target_artifact_2.GetName].
[target_artifact_3.GetName].
On second thought, I will keep them.
The relic will be laid in the shrine forever.
The priests had barely set the reliquary on the altar when the sky split. The relic I promised was not mine to give, and the gods have noticed.
No!
Walls for the Townships

The strategic exclaves of the [target_wonder.GetName] are finished. Every township around [target_province.GetName] now has walls and towers of its own, paid for by the city, and the nearest are joined to it by curtain walls into a single fortress.
Let them come.
Every holding in [target_province.GetName] gets the strongest walls of its kind.
While my men were stripping the [target_wonder.GetName], [target_courtier.GetTitledFirstName] came out carrying [looted_artifact.GetName], and has been showing it off ever since.
Hand it over. It belongs to me.
Keep it, you have earned it.

The looting of the [From.GetName] has begun. Shall my own men strip it, or shall anyone who wants a share be let in? The townsfolk will not forgive us either way, but they will hate us more if they have to watch.
The looting of the [From.GetName] has begun. It is not much of a wonder, and there will not be much to take. Shall my own men strip it, or shall anyone who wants a share be let in?
Only my men. The gold is mine.
Let everyone take what they can carry.
A Stage Stripped
Another part of the [From.GetName] has been torn down and carted away.
There is nothing left of the [From.GetName] worth taking.

The walls of [From.GetName] are breached and the defenders have thrown down their arms. But my soldiers have smelled gold, and they are not waiting for orders. Doors are being kicked in, the first fires are burning, and the screaming has begun.
They have earned it. Let them be.
If they are taking, I am taking.
Hang the first man who disobeys!
Your troops will obey, though some will desert.
Your troops will ignore you.
The whole realm will think you dishonourable.
